# Background

-   Unprecedented urbanization is affecting urban plants, resulting in phenological changes with ecological and societal implications in cities @zhou_understanding_2022.

-   Widely reported phenological changes are based on urban-rural comparisons, attributed to the Urban Heat Island effect @zhou_understanding_2022 @li_response_2017.

-   Treating urban phenology as a uniform entity overlooks the substantial heterogeneity of microclimate and diverse species composition within cities @nilon_routledge_2023 @kong_warming_2025.

## Research questions

1.  How do different individual trees of the same species respond to the thermal variation within a city?

2.  How do these responses differ among cities located in distinct climatic regions across the contiguous United States (CONUS)?

# Methods

## Compiling and consolidating tree inventories

-   Considered the availability of street tree inventories, representative climatic, demographic, and built-environment characteristics.

-   Harmonized taxonomy and restricted the analysis to deciduous trees.

-   Compiled 1,663,951 trees across 113 genera and 345 species from 76 U.S. cities.

```{r}
#| label: data-map
#| include: false
#| warning: false

inventory_centroids <- readRDS(("~/lab-data/datasets/vegetation/StreetTrees/cleaned_ps_input/summary/inventory_centroids.rds"))
boundary_us <- st_read(("~/lab-data/datasets/boundary/USAdministrative/US/us_boundarydissolve.shp"), quiet = T) |> 
  st_transform(4326)

city_feature <- readRDS("~/phenology-urban/data/raw/CONUS/StreetTrees/cleaned_ps_input/summary/city_feature.rds") |>
  select(-bio1, -bio12) |>
  left_join(read_rds("~/phenology-urban/data/raw/CONUS/StreetTrees/cleaned_ps_input/summary/city_bioclimate.rds") |>
              select(site, bio1, bio12), by = "site") |>
  rename(city = site) |>
  mutate(city = ifelse(city == "St_George", "StGeorge", city)) |>
  mutate(city = ifelse(city == "St.Louis", "StLouis", city))


all_city <- readRDS("~/phenology-urban/data/proc/urban/City_list/all_city.rds") |>
  na.omit()
scaled_matrix <- scale(all_city |>
  select(pop_density,bio1, bio12, sd, median)|>
    rename(building_height_sd = sd,
           building_height_median = median)) 
all_city_scaled <- as.data.frame(scaled_matrix)
all_city_scaled$NAME20 <- all_city$NAME20

pca_res <- prcomp(all_city_scaled[, 1:5], center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

pca_scores <- as.data.frame(pca_res$x[, 1:2])
colnames(pca_scores) <- c("PC1", "PC2")
pca_scores$NAME20 <- all_city_scaled$NAME20

pca_loadings <- as.data.frame(pca_res$rotation[, 1:2])
pca_loadings$variable <- rownames(pca_loadings)

arrow_scale <- 5.5
pca_loadings <- pca_loadings |>
  mutate(PC1 = PC1 * arrow_scale,
         PC2 = PC2 * arrow_scale,
         variable = case_when(
    variable == "building_height_sd"     ~ "height_sd",
    variable == "building_height_median" ~ "height_median",
    TRUE ~ variable 
  ))

list_city <- city_feature |>
  st_join(st_read(("~/lab-data/datasets/boundary/USAdministrative/USCities/tl_2024_us_uac20.shp"), quiet = T) |> 
            st_transform(4326) |>
            dplyr::select(NAME20), join = st_nearest_feature) |>
  pull(NAME20)

pca_scores <- pca_scores |>
  mutate(
    selected = NAME20 %in% list_city,
    hover_text = paste("City:", NAME20),
    group = case_when(
      selected ~ "Selected cities",
      TRUE ~ "Other cities"
    )
  )

full_data <- pca_scores |> select(PC1, PC2)
subset_data <- pca_scores |> filter(selected) |> select(PC1, PC2)

density = 0.0001
num_grids = 100
x_breaks <- seq(min(pca_scores$PC1), max(pca_scores$PC1), length.out = num_grids +1)
y_breaks <- seq(min(pca_scores$PC2), max(pca_scores$PC2), length.out = num_grids +1)

df <- pca_scores |>
    mutate(
      x_bin = cut(PC1, breaks = x_breaks, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE),
      y_bin = cut(PC2, breaks = y_breaks, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE),
      grid_id = paste(x_bin, y_bin, sep = "_")
    )
  
grid_full <- expand.grid(
  x_bin = 1:(length(x_breaks) - 1),
  y_bin = 1:(length(y_breaks) - 1)
) |>
  mutate(
    grid_id = paste(x_bin, y_bin, sep = "_"),
    PC1 = (x_breaks[x_bin] + x_breaks[x_bin + 1]) / 2,
    PC2 = (y_breaks[y_bin] + y_breaks[y_bin + 1]) / 2
  ) |>
  left_join(
    df |>
      group_by(x_bin, y_bin) |>
      summarise(count = n(),
                subset = sum(selected),
                .groups = "drop"),
    by = c("x_bin", "y_bin")
  )

kde_full <- kde(x = full_data, eval.points = grid_full |> select(PC1, PC2))
kde_subset <- kde(x = subset_data, eval.points = grid_full|> select(PC1, PC2))

dens_full <- kde_full$estimate / sum(kde_full$estimate)
dens_subset <- kde_subset$estimate / sum(kde_subset$estimate)

grid_df <- cbind(grid_full,
                 full_density = dens_full,
                 subset_density = dens_subset)

contour_df <- grid_df %>%
  select(PC1, PC2, full_density, subset_density) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(full_density, subset_density),
    names_to = "group", values_to = "density"
  ) %>%
  mutate(group = case_when(
    group == "full_density"   ~ "All cities",
    group == "subset_density" ~ "Selected cities",
    TRUE ~ group
  ))
```

## Extracting phenological metrics from PlanetScope @song_ps

-   Retrieved PlanetScope imagery (ortho_analytic_4b_sr) from 2017–2023 and extracted reflectance at tree coordinates.\
-   Constructed smoothed, seasonally reliable Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) curves after computing and filtering EVI time series.
-   Extracted the timing of Start-of-season (SOS) and End-of-season (EOS) as the day of year when the growing-season EVI curves first crossed the green-up/down 50% threshold.

```{r}
#| label: data-evi
#| include: false
#| warning: false
# NY acer rubrum
doy <- read_rds("~/lab-data/datasets/vegetation/PS/CONUS_urban/doy/doy_NewYork_Acerrubrum.rds")|>
  filter(id == 7639) |>
  filter(year == 2023)
clean_ts <- read_rds("~/lab-data/datasets/vegetation/PS/CONUS_urban/clean/clean_NewYork_Acerrubrum.rds") |>
  filter(id == 7639) |>
  filter(date >= as.Date("2022-10-01") & date <= as.Date("2024-3-31"))

df_ts <- clean_ts %>% dplyr::mutate(value_smooth = whittaker_smoothing_filling(evi, lambda = 50))
df_doy <- doy %>%
  dplyr::mutate(date_doy = as.Date(stringr::str_c(year, "-01-01")) + doy - 1,
                date_start = as.Date(stringr::str_c(year, "-01-01")) + start - 1,
                date_end = as.Date(stringr::str_c(year, "-01-01")) + end - 1)
y_min <- min(df_ts$evi, na.rm = TRUE)
y_max <- max(df_ts$evi, na.rm = TRUE)
```

Green and orange shading indicate green-up and green-down periods, with vertical lines marking the 50% thresholds used to define SOS and EOS."
```{r}
#| fig-width: 7

evi <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = df_ts, aes(x = date, y = evi), color = "grey", size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(x = "Time", y = "Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI)") +

    axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 16)
  ) +
  geom_line(data = df_ts, aes(x = date, y = value_smooth), color = "grey40", linewidth = 1.2)+
  geom_segment(data = df_doy |> filter(direction == "up"),
               aes(x = date_doy, xend = date_doy, y = y_min, yend = y_max),
               linewidth = 1.5, col = "dark green", inherit.aes = F) +
  geom_rect(data = df_doy |> filter(direction == "up"),
            aes(xmin = date_start, xmax = date_end, ymin = y_min, ymax = y_max),
            alpha = 0.1,fill = "dark green", inherit.aes = F) +
  geom_segment(data = df_doy |> filter(direction == "down"),
               aes(x = date_doy, xend = date_doy, y = y_min, yend = y_max),
               linewidth = 1.5, col = "orange", inherit.aes = F) +
  geom_rect(data = df_doy |> filter(direction == "down"),
            aes(xmin = date_start, xmax = date_end, ymin = y_min, ymax = y_max),
            alpha = 0.1,fill = "orange", inherit.aes = F) +
  geom_text( data = df_doy |> filter(direction == "up"),
             aes(x = date_doy + 1, y = y_max, label = "SOS = 110"),color = "darkgreen",
             vjust = -0.5,size = 5, inherit.aes = FALSE
) +
geom_text(data = df_doy |> filter(direction == "down"),
          aes(x = date_doy + 1, y = y_max, label = "EOS = 298"),
          color = "orange",vjust = -0.5,size = 5,inherit.aes = FALSE
)
```

## Inferring phenological responses to urban thermal variation

-   Preseason temperature for each tree individual from the U-HAT dataset @uhat_climate.
-   Precipitation and shortwave radiation from the Daymet, used as control variables.
-   Spatial statistical models for each species within each city:

$$y(\mathbf{s}_i, \mathbf{t}_i) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{temp}(\mathbf{s}_i, \mathbf{t}_i) + \beta_2 \text{prcp}(\mathbf{s}_i, \mathbf{t}_i) + \beta_3 \text{srad}(\mathbf{s}_i, \mathbf{t}_i)
+ w(\mathbf{s}_i) + u(\mathbf{t}_i) + \epsilon(\mathbf{s}_i, \mathbf{t}_i)$$

where 

  -   $y(\mathbf{s}_i, \mathbf{t}_i)$ is the phenological timing (SOS or EOS) of tree $i$ located at spatial location $\mathbf{s}_i$ and time $\mathbf{t}_i$.
  
  -   $\text{temp}(\mathbf{s}_i, \mathbf{t}_i)$, $\text{prcp}(\mathbf{s}_i, \mathbf{t}_i)$, and $\text{srad}(\mathbf{s}_i, \mathbf{t}_i)$ are the preseason temperature, precipitation, and shortwave radiation, respectively.
  
  -   $w(\mathbf{s}_i)$ is the spatial random effect modeled using a Gaussian Process to account for spatial autocorrelation, modeled using a Matérn covariance structure.
  
  -   $u(\mathbf{t}_i)$ is the temporal random effect capturing year-to-year variability.
  
  -   $\epsilon(\mathbf{s}_i, \mathbf{t}_i)$ is the residual error term.

  -   **$\beta_1$ is the coefficient for the average temperature, which is the main interest of this study**.

```{r}
#| label: data-ny-temp
#| include: false
source(here("script/spatial_stats_model/prepare_model_input.R"))
species = "Acer rubrum"
phe_type = "SOS"
phe_metric <- "doy"

model_input_sf <-  prepare_data("NewYork", source = "Grid", taxa_col= "canonicalname", phe_type = phe_type)|>
  filter(canonicalname == species)

x <- model_input_sf[[phe_metric]]
q <- stats::quantile(x, probs = c(0.25, 0.75), na.rm = TRUE)
iqr <- diff(q)
lo  <- q[1] - 1.5 * iqr
hi  <- q[2] + 1.5 * iqr
NY_city_input <- model_input_sf %>%
  filter(is.na(.data[[phe_metric]]) |
           dplyr::between(.data[[phe_metric]], lo, hi))
  
tree_location <- NY_city_input |>
  filter(year == 2023) |>
  filter(!(lon == "NaN") & !(lat == "NaN")) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326, remove = F)

file <- "~/lab-data/datasets/climate/UHAT/clean/NewYork_winter_2023.tif"
temp_tif <- terra::rast(file)
tifs <- list.files(
  "~/lab-data/datasets/climate/UHAT/grid",
  pattern = "^MYD11A1\\..*LST_Day_1km\\.tif$",
  full.names = TRUE
)
r_template <- terra::rast(tifs[1])
crs(temp_tif) <- crs(r_template)  # ensure correct CRS
tree_location <- tree_location|>
  st_transform(crs(temp_tif))

clipped <- crop(temp_tif, vect(tree_location))
temp_df <- as.data.frame(clipped, xy = TRUE) |>
  rename_with(~ "value", .cols = 3)

bbox <- st_bbox(tree_location)

## change to model fit and point density

Acer_rubrum_SOS <- readRDS("~/phenology-urban/data/proc/model_output/final_models_clean_outlier/inla/spatial_spde/NewYork/canonicalname/Acer_rubrum_SOS.rds")

b0     <- Acer_rubrum_SOS$res$summary.fixed["Intercept", "mean"]
b_temp <- Acer_rubrum_SOS$res$summary.fixed["temp",      "mean"]
b_prcp <- Acer_rubrum_SOS$res$summary.fixed["prcp",      "mean"]
b_srad <- Acer_rubrum_SOS$res$summary.fixed["srad",      "mean"]
u_2023 <- Acer_rubrum_SOS$res$summary.random$year[
           Acer_rubrum_SOS$res$summary.random$year$ID=="2023","mean"]
sd_b0     <- Acer_rubrum_SOS$res$summary.fixed["Intercept", "sd"]
sd_b_temp <- Acer_rubrum_SOS$res$summary.fixed["temp",      "sd"]
sd_b_prcp <- Acer_rubrum_SOS$res$summary.fixed["prcp",      "sd"]
sd_b_srad <- Acer_rubrum_SOS$res$summary.fixed["srad",      "sd"]
u_2023_sd <- Acer_rubrum_SOS$res$summary.random$year[
  Acer_rubrum_SOS$res$summary.random$year$ID == "2023", "sd"
]

mean_prcp <- mean(NY_city_input$prcp_winter, na.rm = TRUE)
mean_srad <- mean(NY_city_input$srad_winter, na.rm = TRUE)
temp_seq <- seq(
  min(NY_city_input$temp_winter, na.rm = TRUE),
  max(NY_city_input$temp_winter, na.rm = TRUE),
  length.out = 200
)

# 5. Predicted y for year=2023
y_mean_2023 <- b0 + b_temp * temp_seq +
               b_prcp * mean_prcp +
               b_srad * mean_srad +
               u_2023   # <-- add random effect
eta_var <- sd_b0^2 +
  (temp_seq^2)       * sd_b_temp^2 +
  (mean_prcp^2)      * sd_b_prcp^2 +
  (mean_srad^2)      * sd_b_srad^2 +
  u_2023_sd^2

eta_sd <- sqrt(eta_var)

# 95% CI
z_975 <- qnorm(0.975)
y_lower_2023 <- y_mean_2023 - z_975 * eta_sd
y_upper_2023 <- y_mean_2023 + z_975 * eta_sd

plot_data <- data.frame(
  temp   = temp_seq,
  y_mean = y_mean_2023,
  y_low  = y_lower_2023,
  y_high = y_upper_2023
)
```

```{r}
           expand = FALSE) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12),

    legend.key.height = unit(0.3, "cm"),
    legend.key.width  = unit(0.4, "cm"), 
    legend.title = element_text(size = 8),

    legend.spacing.y = unit(0.1, "cm")
  )

sp_ny_scatter_plot <- ggplot() +
  geom_hex(data = NY_city_input, aes(x = temp_winter, y = doy), bins = 60, alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "grey70", 
    high = "grey10" 
  ) +
  geom_ribbon(data = plot_data, aes(x = temp, y = y_mean, ymin = y_low, ymax = y_high), fill = "#FCA636FF", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(data = plot_data, aes(x = temp, y = y_mean), color = "#FCA636FF", linewidth = 1) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14)+
  labs(x = "Mean winter temperature (°C)", 
       y = "Start-of-season (DOY)") +
  theme_classic() +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = -Inf, y = -Inf,     
    label = paste0("hat(beta)[temp] == ", round(b_temp, 2)),
    hjust = -0.5, vjust = -0.6, 
    size  = 6,
    color = "#FCA636FF",
    parse = TRUE
  )+
  theme(
```

# Results

## Tree phenology responds to fine-scale temperature heterogeneity

-   Temperature effects on phenology are common but strongly species-specific in direction and magnitude. 
-   EOS responses are more consistent than SOS, with predominantly positive effects suggesting delayed senescence under warmer urban conditions.

```{r}
#| include: false
# Helper to process files by pattern
plot_coef_sp_city <- function(r_output_dir){
  coef_summary <- data.frame()
  coef_summary <- map_dfr(
      phe_types,
      ~ read_rds(paste0(r_output_dir, .x, "_summary.rds")) %>%
          mutate(phe_type = .x)
    )
  coef_summary$Factor2 <- factor(coef_summary$Factor,
                               levels = unique(coef_summary$Factor))
  coef_summary$phe_type <- factor(coef_summary$phe_type,
                                levels = c("SOS", "EOS"))
  p_coef <-  ggplot(coef_summary, aes(x = Factor2, 
                               y = Estimate,
                               color = Color
                               )) +
    geom_point(aes(alpha = SigAlpha, color = Color), position = position_dodge(w = 0.5), size = 3) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Lower, ymax = Upper, alpha = SigAlpha, color = Color), 
                  position = position_dodge(w = 0.5), 
                  width = 0.2) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
    labs(x = "Species", y = bquote(beta[Temp]~" estimate")) + 
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 75, hjust = 1, size = 8, face = "italic"),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 14)) +
    # coord_flip() +
    facet_wrap(~ phe_type, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_alpha_identity() +
    scale_color_identity() +
    # geom_text(aes(label = Sig, y = Upper + 0.05  ), hjust = -0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
    # geom_text(aes(label = Estimate, y = Estimate  ), vjust = -0.7, show.legend = FALSE, size = 3) +
    guides(alpha = "none")
  
  return(p_coef)
}
```

## Phenological responses vary with regional climatic context

-   As for city-level average response, EOS shows stronger sensitivity than SOS, with larger variation among species.
-   Cities in CA and FL display a consistent pattern of delayed spring and advanced fall phenology with warming. In contrast, much of the central and eastern U.S. shows the opposite response.
-   Higher temperatures tend to delay EOS in wetter cities but accelerate it in drier ones.

```{r}
#| label: data-marginal
#| warning: false
#| include: false
plot_marginal <- function(species_name, coef_summary_all, clim = "mean_temp", phe_type = "EOS") {
  if(clim %in% c("mean_prcp", "mean_temp")) {
    new_city_feature <-  read_rds(paste0("~/phenology-urban/data/proc/model_output/nooutlier_", phe_type, "_input.rds")) |>
    filter(year < 2024) |>
    mutate(year = as.factor(year))|>
    filter(canonicalname == species_name) |>
    group_by(city) |>
    summarise(
      across(starts_with("temp"), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE), .names = "mean_temp"),
      across(starts_with("prcp"), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE), .names = "mean_prcp"))
  } else if (clim %in% c("bio1", "bio12")) {
    new_city_feature <- readRDS("~/phenology-urban/data/raw/CONUS/StreetTrees/cleaned_ps_input/summary/city_bioclimate.rds") |>
      select(site, all_of(clim)) |>
      rename(city = site)
    
  } else {
    stop("clim variable not recognized")
  }
  
  
  combine_feature <- coef_summary_all |>
    filter(Factor == species_name) |>
    mutate(w = 1/(sd^2)) |>
    left_join(
      new_city_feature,
      by = "city"
    )

  df_eos <- combine_feature |>
    filter(phe_type == !!phe_type)

  if (nrow(df_eos) < 2) return(NULL)

  # lm
  fmla <- as.formula(paste0("Estimate ~ ", clim))
  fit_w <- lm(fmla, data = df_eos, weights = w)

  summary_fit <- summary(fit_w)
  R2   <- summary_fit$r.squared
  pval <- summary_fit$coefficients[2, 4]
  label_text <- sprintf("italic(p) == %.3f", pval)

  # interval
  newdat <- data.frame(
    clim_var = seq(min(df_eos[[clim]], na.rm = TRUE),
                   max(df_eos[[clim]], na.rm = TRUE),
                   length.out = 200)
  )
  names(newdat) <- clim

  pred <- predict(fit_w, newdata = newdat, se.fit = TRUE)
  newdat$y_pred <- pred$fit
  newdat$y_lwr  <- pred$fit - 1.96 * pred$se.fit
  newdat$y_upr  <- pred$fit + 1.96 * pred$se.fit

  # plot
  p <- ggplot(df_eos, aes(x = .data[[clim]], y = Estimate, alpha = SigAlpha)) +
    geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = Lower, ymax = Upper, colour = Color)) +
    geom_ribbon(data = newdat,
                aes(x = .data[[clim]], ymin = y_lwr, ymax = y_upr),
                inherit.aes = FALSE,
                fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_line(data = newdat,
              aes(x = .data[[clim]], y = y_pred),
              inherit.aes = FALSE,
              colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.8) +
    annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf,
             label = label_text, parse = TRUE,
             hjust = 1.2, vjust = 1.5, size = 6) +
    scale_alpha_identity() +
    scale_colour_identity() +
    guides(alpha = "none") +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      title = species_name,
      x = case_when(
        (rlang::as_name(clim) %in% c("mean_prcp", "bio12")) ~ "Mean Annual Precipitation (mm)",
        (rlang::as_name(clim) %in% c("mean_temp", "bio1")) ~ "Mean Annual Temperature (°C)"
      ),
      y = paste0("Estimated effect on ", phe_type)
    ) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 22),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 16),
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      title = element_text(face = "italic")
    )

  return(p)
}
```

## Discussion

-   Warming generally advances SOS due to forcing accumulation, but insufficient chilling can delay SOS, especially in warm cities @yang_chiling_2023.
-   Water availability can mitigate drought stress during the growing season, allowing trees to senesce later under warming conditions @chen_leaf_2020.
-   Large variance in EOS might be due to multiple, strongly species-specific processes, including heat and drought stress, water-use strategies, and nutrient retranslocation @piao_review_2019.

# Conclusions & Future work

-   Fine‐scale phenological responses to intra‐urban temperature variation are widespread across cities and species.
-   The magnitude of these responses is linked to the broader regional climate context, particularly reflected by the positive association between the EOS–temperature sensitivity and the mean annual precipitation.
-   Explore the physiological mechanism behind the senescence-temperature sensitivity.
